thread:
Anna (Design): uploaded a quick WIP of the model latency dashboard — can you skim? wondering specifically about legend placement, units on the y-axis, and how we handle spikes :eyes:
figma-bot: screenshot uploaded — https://redwood.design/figma/latency-dashboard-wip
Josh (Eng): looks good. quick thought: are we showing ms or seconds? current data has values that span 5ms to 4s so units matter for readability
Anna (Design): yeah — debating showing ms for everything vs switching to s when >1000ms. Also thinking about showing small smoothed line + raw points for outliers
Tejas (Product): as a PM, I'd prefer one consistent unit per chart. users get confused when units flip. maybe a unit toggle in the top-right? :thinking_face:
Liam (Data Viz): consistent unit is simpler. Alternative: use SI prefixes (e.g., 50 ms, 1.2 s) with a compact formatter. Keeps scale interpretable while retaining precision
Ravi (Accessibility): a11y nits: legend colors need 4.5:1 contrast vs background when in light mode, and keyboard focus should be able to cycle legend entries to toggle series. Also tooltips need aria descriptions not just visual text
Anna (Design): good call. for legend placement, I'm torn between right-side vertical legend vs inline top-left. Right-side eats space at narrow widths though
Josh (Eng): technical note: right-side legend is easier to implement with our current grid (we reserve a column). but for mobile it's messy. We could collapse it into a top bar on small breakpoints
Liam (Data Viz): top-inline legend works for 2-3 series. For many series, consider an overflow menu. Also show small swatches with text label on hover for clarity
Tejas (Product): what about smoothing? customers complained smoothing hides regressions in last week's feedback. we need an explicit toggle and callout when smoothing is on
Anna (Design): agree — propose default OFF, and a small pill that says "Smoothing: On" when enabled with tooltip explaining window size
Josh (Eng): implementation: we can do a rolling median or low-pass. rolling median is better for spikes. pseudocode:
```
rolling_median(values, window=5)
```
but it's heavier CPU on large series, we can run it server-side on aggregated windows
Liam (Data Viz): for outliers, don't clip silently. Options: 1) show break in axis (indicate with zig-zag), 2) cap axis and show outlier badges ("+3 points > 2s"), 3) render raw points with lower alpha. I prefer #2 for dashboards where baseline matters
Ravi (Accessibility): if you do "+3 points" badge, ensure it's reachable by keyboard and has aria-label like "3 outliers above 2 seconds". Also the zig-zag axis needs an accessible text description of the scale jump
Anna (Design): noted. copy tweaks: badge copy should be short — maybe "3 spikes > 2s". and tooltips should include exact timestamps and request id when available
Tejas (Product): product ask: add a unit selector (ms / s / auto) in the top-right so power users can switch. default auto uses SI formatting Liam suggested
Josh (Eng): perf: rendering raw points for long traces (100k points) will tank client. need to do progressive downsampling and fetch full-resolution on hover/zoom
Liam (Data Viz): yes — include a zoom+pan detail view. main chart shows downsampled line + outlier badges. clicking zoom fetches timeseries tile w/ raw points
Anna (Design): accessibility color palette: can we pick a palette with 6 colors that meet contrast? Ravi — can you propose a token set we can use across console charts
Ravi (Accessibility): will do. I'll post a PR with tokens and contrast ratios. also recommend an alternate pattern for color-blind: add distinct marker shapes or dashed lines for series differentiation
Anna (Design): last: legend interactions — keyboard: focus moves to legend item, Enter toggles series, Space opens color picker. hover states show 3px stroke width. are we ok with that UX
Josh (Eng): fine from infra side. color picker might need permissions gating but UI-wise OK
Tejas (Product): one more: copy for axis label should be explicit: "Latency (ms)" or "Latency (s)" not just "Latency". helps new users
Anna (Design): great. I'll iterate: - default unit auto w/ SI formatting - smoothing OFF by default + visible pill + tooltip - outlier badges with accessible aria-labels - legend top-inline on narrow screens, right-side on desktop with overflow menu for many series - keyboard interactions + color tokens PR from Ravi
Liam (Data Viz): if you want I can sketch a few variants for the legend and the badge microcopy tomorrow
Anna (Design): please do, thanks! planning to update Figma and post a new screenshot by EOD :thumbsup:
figma-bot: Anna updated file "latency-dashboard-wip" (v3)
Josh (Eng): quick follow-up: can we add a tiny subtitle under chart title that shows the active unit & smoothing state? will help avoid confusion when users copy screenshots
Anna (Design): yea will add subtitle: e.g., "Unit: auto • Smoothing: off"
Tejas (Product): thanks everyone — this is helpful. we'll fold into the next dashboard sprint
Ravi (Accessibility): I'll attach the color token PR and a short checklist for QA once you push the new mockups
Anna (Design): awesome. done for now, will ping when new mockups are in. :)
